SourceString: \"High Priestess,\r\n\r\nWe have eliminated most of the meddling members of the Order of Prometheus, as the mistress instructed, and the survivors have been driven into hiding. They will not interfere.\"

\"Quartermistress,\r\n\r\nAre you certain that the Goddess allowed the half-man beasts into the temple? Surely they are not worthy of serving alongside us? And... must I say it? The stench is... unpleasant.\"
\"High Priestess,\r\n\r\nI hope that Centaurus\' bestial brutes know how to take orders. Chaos in the ranks is the last thing we need, if the God-Marked truly is approaching.\"
\"The beast-men are ideal fodder to tire out the God-Marked before we close in for the kill.\"
\"...the difficulties he has in cultivating exotic plants are of no consequence to me. The sisters require the finest poisons, no matter the difficulties in cultivating them...\"
The scroll is filled with feverish scrawling:\r\n\r\n\"...Oh Daughter of Nyx! Dispenser of Dues! See my devotion! Hear my prayers! I give my life, my soul my heart to you...\"

"Centaurus is the first of the Ixionidae, the son of the demigod descendent of Ares, Ixion, and the divine cloud mother, Nephele. He inherited a spark of divinity from them, leaving him incredibly strong and untouched by age or time.

The rest of us, those Nephele birthed after him, or those in later generations, lack this spark, ageing and dying as mortal men do. 

Centaurus may not be a full god, and can indeed be killed, but he has the potential to live forever, guiding our people into the ages to come."

"The Brandbearers have caused an uproar by claiming that 'Chiron is not a true centaur!'

They are correct.

I may look like you, but I am not a descendent of Ixion, or Centaurus, the first true centaur, who your people are named after.

My father is--unfortunately--Kronos, the mad Titan of Time, and I was born long before Ixion or Nephele ever existed. I am no mortal.

So... if a 'centaur' is one of the lineage of Centaurus, then no, I am not a centaur.

But if there is one thing I have learned in my long years, is that our origins matter far less than who we choose as our family. I choose you all. I am honored that you have chosen me."

This old scroll's faded words are barely visible:

"Welcome, travelers and traders to sunny Pelagora!

All merchants from across Arkadia, or even beyond, are welcome here, to trade with low taxes and..."

This old message has been preserved in the dry air:

"Nicanor,

Nemesis requests that you provide her with another set of a dozen living statues to guard her temple. She has found your skills most satisfactory."
\"Bring the living beneath my statue\'s shadow. Their sacrifce becomes your reward.\"
\"Bring the living beneath my statue\'s shadow. Their sacrifce becomes your reward.\"
\"Bring the living beneath my statue\'s shadow. Their sacrifce becomes your reward.\"
Herein lies a reminder of Iapetos, the foolish titan of mortality. Come close to death, but live and fight, if you wish to enter.
In the shadow of the tree, strike times three. Five times again at the stones among flowers. Then twice here to access Koios\'s chamber.
A trick of light to enter Hyperion\'s chamber. Bring forth the blue moon\'s reflection.
For the light which Hyperion loved most, bring here that of the yellow sun.
\"The Titans ruled before Olympos—giants of unchecked force. Their reign scarred heaven and earth alike, until a mighty king shattered Kronos\'s power and bound his kin to eternal silence.\"

“Hyperion, that dim and sputtering Titan, once dared to drag the sun across the sky as if he commanded its flame. The chamber to the east stands as a reminder of his stolen glow—an echo of radiance he never earned.”

“________, that dim and sputtering Titan, once dared to drag the sun across the sky as if he commanded its flame. The chamber to the east stands as a reminder of his stolen glow—an echo of radiance he never earned.”
“Fancying himself the axis of the heavens, Koios did nothing more than skulk in the shadow of scrolls and whisper half‑truths to my father. His knowledge is reduced to the northern chamber alone.\"
“Fancying himself the axis of the heavens, _____ did nothing more than skulk in the shadow of scrolls and whisper half‑truths to my father. His knowledge is reduced to the northern chamber alone.\"
\"The chamber of Iapetos is to the west. He was a dreary Titan who fancied himself the master of mortality, strutting around as though he shaped the fate of mortals.\"
\"The chamber of _______ is to the west. He was a dreary Titan who fancied himself the master of mortality, strutting around as though he shaped the fate of mortals.\"
\"Should anyone but me hold dominion over the constellations - those night sky memorials? I say the chamber in the south will be the only memorial for Krios, that pompous star‑herder.\"
“I tore–from Kronos’s trembling–ended the age of cowardice–”
“When I rose, the sky itself shuddered, for it knew a true king had come.”
“The Titans boasted of strength–broke like rotted pillars–”
“I hurled Kronos–past earth and root–pit where only failure–”
“--roars shook the deep–my chains held firmer–”
\"–that felled Ouranos–buried by my decree–unfit for any hand–\"
“I sealed that cursed–for it carves ruin–cosmos alike.”
“If ever that edge–world will shudder–stored it beyond–reach.\"
“I, Zeus, struck Kronos with lightning so fierce the sky split. His ancient rule finally burned away, his fate completed.”
“From his fallen grip I took the sickle—power too great to be weilded by anyone.”
“I drove the Titans screaming into Tartaros, sealing their defeat and my unchallenged rule.”
\"The Order of Prometheus must be praised for what they accomplished in removing this power from the Telkines.\"
\"Hmmm... Should I turn my attention to the Temple of the Hidden Sun?\"
\"Triangle, then square, then star... but how many of each?\"
Only a few phrases remain legible on this stone.\r\n\r\n\"...bring their bodies to the flames...burn like their father...ashes from centaur pyres remain forever in the Chamber...\"
A centaur\'s corpse, covered in spider bites.
A note on this corpse looks quickly scrawled. \r\n\r\n\"Ancestors angry. Attacking. What caused this madness? Ixion\'s murder?\"

This blood-stained and faded record is barely legible.

"Notes of Machaon, Order of Prometheus:

Day 86: Her numbers have grown. Why would Nemesis need so many priestesses?

Day 151: I've seen strange events unfurl. Priestesses arresting other priestesses, dragging them off to some dungeon.

Day 310: I may be compromised. It was reckless to keep returning to this vantage point, but only from here could I witness priestesses training like assassins. I'll leave for Sparta tomorrow."

Clenched in the fist is a letter: 

"We avoid the spiders, find the rumored treasure, and get out of there.Then we live anywhere we want. 

But no matter what, we find the treasure first. 

Oh, and I love you.

--Metriche"
A Brandbearer barely stirs inside this cage, bruised and weak. He says nothing, but his eyes track you.
A few mangy and half-starved felines look past you as if you weren\'t even there.
This caged boarman looks terrified and desperate to flee.
The spiders seem reluctant to approach the cage door.
\"We left Pelion’s slopes with storm‑hearts, following Centaurus toward Ixion’s echoing throne.\"
\"Hooves thundered westward as we sought the father who claimed us.\"
“The journey to Ixion’s halls broke the weak; only the fiercest survived the endless stone valleys.”
“Humans once loyal to Ixion fled at our arrival, their faith brittle as autumn straw.”
“Human betrayal sickened Centaurus, who swore their lands would remember his fury for all ages.”
“The first clash stained the grass black; humans fell quickly beneath hooves trained on the slopes of Pelion.”
“The last human village to fall was where we finally found rest. Centaurus called this place Sanctuary.”
“For generations we ruled the wilderness—feral and triumphant—until Chiron brought gentler wisdom.”
“Sophoi led in times of peace, but war required the bloody hooves of the Brandbearers.”
“Now the Sophoi and Brandbearers argue over destiny, each claiming Pelion’s legacy as their truth.”
“...human youths, welcomed by Chiron as students. He claims wisdom grows stronger when shared beyond the herd.”
“But teaching humans dilutes our strength. It softens our hooves - hooves born for war!”
“Human heroes train beside us, learning spearwork and healing; many centaurs question why humans deserve such gifts.”
“Chiron insists knowledge has no tribe, though this angers those still loyal to Centaurus - those of Ixion\'s blood.”
“Rumors spread that humans use Chiron’s lessons against us, like Theseus, who expelled us from Mount Pelion so many centuries ago.”

"Difficult to access, this ruined fortress of Helios will be the perfect place for our little game. 

We sell them idols to bring to the Kinslayer's Fire and reward the few winners. They encourage others to buy idols for a chance to win, and we split the profits. 

The losers? Well, no one will ever hear from them again."
-- Sippas

"Sippas, the fools love their games, don't they? Selling worthless items to burn for a chance to win prizes... or die? Wickedly brilliant! 

And this place is perfect for storing all our profits and inventory! I might get rid of those wolf statues though - they're a bit of an eye-sore to me."
-- Mippas

"These hideous half-men, half-horse abominations cannot be bested by normal means - we know that now. 

And so I lend my talents to something even more grotesque: a sacrifice of so many to drive these invaders back to Pelion. Forgive me. 

- Priest Meurius"
Golden flowers rise up, full of life and energy as if the soil itself is thrumming with power.
A coppery smell emanates from them, almost like blood.
These blood-colored flowers reach up to the sky, strong and vital.
The petals of this plant pulse gently when you approach.
Words have been scrawled onto the side of this statue.\r\n\r\n\"A ring, a ring of pillars you seek. Within, within you will follow the meek.\"

An exotic recipe is written here with a few items already crossed out:

"Boil the following in order:
- <st>Twig of a Hamadryad</>
- <st>Hair from a Centaur Mane</>
- <st>Tusk of Boarman</>  <i>- Gored me; hope it doesn't fester.</>
- <st>Hippokampus Scale</>
- Bitter Leaf x 3 <i>- Haven't found any yet, and feeling weak...</>"
\"Our forefather\'s killer walks freely among our lands. A great reward will be granted to any who bring this murderer\'s head to the war camp!\"

A hastily-written message, posted for all:\r\n\r\n\"The Sanctuary of the Sophoi is a den of weakness and heresy. They welcome Ixion\'s killer; they betray centaur-kind. Take up your weapons and join us in overthrowing Thespios and the Sophoi!\"

Someone carved a message in this rock: 

"To the northeast, outside the wall,
Between four bull heads mounted tall,
We'll store what we own and await the day,
We can be together and run away."
A centaur killed by either the surrounding poison, or the knife in his side.
This centaur appears to have succumbed to the poison in the air, surrounded by gold. His knife sheath is empty.
This vow belongs to a priestess named <gold>Lena</> and appears to have a tiny, delicate plant inside.
A priestess named <gold>Elena</> made this vow. The blood inside seems strangely calming, steadying the mind.
The name <gold>Nikolina</> appears on this green and yellow ampule, but only when candlelight is behind it.
The blood in this ampule looks more purple than red. The name <gold>Lisa</> is etched on the glass.
This blood vow is wrapped in loops of soft, orange yarn, but the name of whomever made it is nowhere to be found.
Shocking to the touch, this blood vow has the name <gold>Electra</> on it.
Possibly the first vow created - you have to wipe away the dust of years to see the name <gold>Rhebekka</>.
A statue of a priestess in good condition. Probably a reminder of who is in control here.
\"Claimed Nemesis was trying to leave her own service. You really can\'t trust much anyone says past a certain point of pain.\r\n\r\n-- Interrogator Ino\"
\"This one screamed more than others. Do certain individuals feel more pain? I should compare notes with some of the healers. \r\n\r\n-- Interrogator Ino\"

\"I sometimes wonder if I\'ve crossed a line in my interrogations, I really do. But then a prisoner will say something so unthinkably bad about the mistress and I realize I\'ve probably been too lenient.\r\n\r\n-- Interrogator Ino\"

\"My key no longer seems to open this door. While my work does not include visiting the Blood Vows, I will <i>not</> be made to look like a fool should the High Priestess arrive for an inspection. Make it work or else.\r\n\r\n-- Interrogator Ino\"
\"I think something might be wrong with Interrogator Ino\'s methods. Almost everyone she questions dies terribly.\r\n\r\n-- Interrogator Lasthena\"

"Surprise inspections of the dungeons and all territories belonging to our Mistress Nemesis should be expected at any time. 

And remember: a failed inspection will not be tolerated.

-- High Priestess Electra"
This scroll, like so many of the ones in this room, contains an exhaustive list of names of recruited priestesses.
\"Undeniably, our goddess, Nemesis, has the first and last word in retribution. What she says is unquestionably correct.\"
\"<st>Every punishment should be just.</> Every Punishment determined by Nemesis <i>is</> just.\"
\"If in doubt, use imprisonment until a superior priestess passes judgement. Should that be impossible, use lethal force.\"
These stones are weathered, but once finely carved - each a devotion a past centaur carried and placed here.
One of several statues memorializing the first centaurs who attempted the pilgrimage.
Sophoi leatherwork for armor and wrapping weapons. The Sophoi may value wisdom, but they\'re clearly not pacifists.
It looks as though the Sophoi revere their equine heritage.
This looks like an ancient place of worship, but there are small signs it might still be used in a similar way.
A statue that many who once lived here no doubt prayed to for protection.
This stone\'s engravings may have once told of this land\'s history, but most of the symbols are chipped or worn away.
Tools, which may have once been proudly owned, show rust and pitting from lack of use.
The face of a once-great king or hero from the past, whose name is lost in time.
The Brandbearers seem to admire the ancient breed of Magnesian Mares.
Skulls, carved runes, and the smell of decay. Perhaps a sacrificial site, or a warning to trespassers.
\"Always remember - Herakles may have killed the river guardian, but Nessus had his revenge by fooling the human hero\'s wife.\"
\"Between a hero and a hero\'s destiny, no wall - man-made or otherwise, can stand.\"
\"Before any test of skill, there is always a phase of preparation. \r\n\r\nIn this instance, it will be gathering the required amount of Guardian Cores.\"
This beautiful sculpture never made it to its destination.
